svg.title: A merge request that only changes deployment files does not wait for the test suite: The test suite is skipped only when every changed file is a deployment file
svg.text: A merge request that only changes deployment files does
not wait for the test suite
Scenario: The test suite is skipped only when every changed file is a deployment file
A release that only moves image tags
Anything else still runs the test suite
When in doubt, the test suite runs
A single file, not a whole folder

g.text: Given a merge request that changes nothing but an image tag in a deployment folder
A project keeps its deployment in two folders, project/kustomize and project/argocd, next to its code in project/src and
its test in project/tests. The terminal lists them first.
This merge request ships version 1.5.0. git diff shows the whole change: the two image tags of the production overlay
move from 1.4.0 to 1.5.0, and nothing else.
Then with no deployment folder named, the test suite runs as before
The setting ships empty in .env.dist, so a project that never heard of it keeps its pipeline as it was. The grep shows
the empty line.
The script says "The test suite runs: TASK_DEVSECOPS_TEST_DEPLOY_PATHS is empty." and ends on exit code 1, which tells a
legacy caller to run the suite.
Then once the main branch names the deployment folders, the same merge request skips the
test suite
The main branch now names the two folders in .env.dist, as the first line shows. The same merge request still changes
one file, the production overlay.
This time the script says "Only deployment files changed (project/kustomize project/argocd): the test suite is skipped."
and ends on exit code 0. A legacy caller can stop there.

text.tspan: git show main:.env.dist | grep '^TASK_DEVSECOPS_TEST_DEPLOY_PATHS='; git diff --stat main...HEAD;

g.text: Then a merge request that also changes a test runs the test suite
The same release also touches a test: git diff lists two files. One of them, project/tests/app.test.js, is outside the
deployment folders, and that is enough.
The script names that file and the suite runs: exit code 1.

text.tspan: git diff --stat main...HEAD; CI_MERGE_REQUEST_DIFF_BASE_SHA=$(git rev-parse main) bash

g.text: Then a merge request that changes the setting itself runs the test suite
A merge request cannot use the setting to skip its own tests. Here it adds project/src to the deployment folders, as the
two diff lines show, and changes project/src/app.js in the same push.
The script reads the change against the main branch. .env.dist is one of the changed files and sits outside the
deployment folders, so the script names it and the suite runs: exit code 1.

text.tspan: git diff main...HEAD -- .env.dist | grep '^[-+]TASK_DEVSECOPS_TEST_DEPLOY_PATHS='; git diff --stat main...HEAD;

g.text: Then outside a merge request the test suite always runs
GitLab sets CI_MERGE_REQUEST_DIFF_BASE_SHA only on a merge request pipeline. Without it, on the main branch, on a tag or
on a schedule, there is no merge request to compare.
This is the same change that skipped the suite two chapters ago. Run without a merge request around it, the script says
"this is not a merge request pipeline." and the suite runs: exit code 1.
Then when the change cannot be computed the test suite runs
The diff base points to a commit this clone does not hold, so git cannot say what changed. The script does not guess: it
says "cannot compute the diff" and the suite runs, exit code 1.
Then once the main branch names a single file, a merge request that only changes that file
skips the test suite
The main branch now names one file instead of two folders: the production overlay, as the first line shows. The merge
request is the same release, one file.
The script says "Only deployment files changed (project/kustomize/overlays/production/kustomization.yaml): the test
suite is skipped." and ends on exit code 0.

text.tspan: git show main:.env.dist | grep '^TASK_DEVSECOPS_TEST_DEPLOY_PATHS='; git diff --stat main...HEAD;

g.text: Then a new file next to the named file runs the test suite
The same release also adds a file next to the overlay, project/kustomize/overlays/production/ingress.yaml. The setting
names the overlay, not its folder, so the new file is not a deployment file.
The script names the new file and the suite runs: exit code 1.

text.tspan: git diff --stat main...HEAD; CI_MERGE_REQUEST_DIFF_BASE_SHA=$(git rev-parse main) bash

g.text: Then legacy callers can skip while current CI jobs execute their tasks
The standalone helper still accepts an exported deployment list and can skip a legacy/local caller. Current build, test
and deploy jobs execute their tasks whenever GitLab creates them.

svg.text: Storyboard e2e · 10 steps · 10 frames · every frame is its own pixel baseline (tolerance: 0)
● Given: stage ● When: actions ● Then: proofs
